claims.statement: useGame opens a single useStream on the `chess` assistant per game, and every submit carries configurable built by configurableOf from the game's record (the settings version first, then every setting key in order, nothing else; DEFAULT_CONTEXT only as a stand-in when there is no record), run_name chess-web with tag web, metadata surface web, and multitaskStrategy reject.

The web UI stores the current game's thread id in the `thread` URL query parameter via history.replaceState; when useStream reports a new thread id and the hook is still mounted, it binds the id and writes it to the URL, and the browser stores nothing per game because the game's setup lives in the thread.

On load, App seats the thread found in the URL with no chosen record so its setup comes from the thread; a new game or rematch clears the URL thread and creates a seat with a higher number and a chosen side and context (a rematch swaps sides and keeps the context), remounting the keyed Table so useStream starts a fresh thread, and a seat where the human plays Black auto-sends `go` once on mount guarded by a ref.

Human commands get message ids memoized per hook instance (one game) by the key ply:content, deliberately excluding the thread id because a new game's first command is sent before a thread exists, so a resend of the same command at the same position reuses the id, which the server treats as a no-op for already-consumed ids.

useGame's play sends the UCI move as a human message with an optimistic pendingMove shown until the submit settles, start sends `go`, and retry submits empty input to resume a pending turn because a fresh `go` is rejected while a turn is pending.

The Table locks the board when the game has no record or has not finished loading, when viewing an earlier ply, while loading, after the game ends, while a turn is pending, or while an optimistic move is in flight, and it swallows the SDK's 'a run is already in flight' rejection while surfacing other submit errors.

Auth failures (HTTP status 401/403, or SDK request messages anchored at the start as HTTP/Protocol/Thread state request failures with 401/403, so a model provider's 401 inside a run does not match) show a banner directing the user to Settings, where the only app-level setting is the LangSmith API key stored under langchain-chess:app and passed to useStream.

Pressing Play in the New game dialog first checks the API key by POSTing to /assistants/search: 401/403 is 'missing' without a key and 'rejected' with one, a network failure is 'unreachable', and anything else is ok; the game starts only on ok and only if the picks on screen are unchanged and still playable, and a late answer after unmount is ignored.

matchupOf derives the policy from the dialog picks (hybrid with both System 1 and an LLM, otherwise systemone or llm), rejects picking neither, an empty custom model spec, model_kwargs the server would hold back when an LLM plays, or an LLM game with memory on while the model's limit is being checked or could not be checked, turns memory off for a model without a known limit, and fills the unused model field with its default; a Random side is resolved once when Play is pressed.
With no game on screen the New game dialog cannot be closed, and opening Settings from it preserves the unsaved picks as a draft that is restored on return.

The server exposes GET /ui/config returning the graph id, JSON schema and defaults of ChessContext, but no frontend fetches it; the settings types, specs, labels, help and defaults are compiled in from chess-ui's generated settings, and the web app's CONTEXT_CHECKS is derived from the generated SETTING_SPECS.

localStorage holds only the last New game setup, the API key and the reply-card view toggles; stored setups are untrusted: they carry their settings version, a setup without a version loads as the defaults, knobs are migrated from their version with unknown keys dropped and each invalid value falls back to its own default, and an unreadable version trusts no stored knob.

apiUrl uses VITE_API_URL if set, otherwise http://localhost:2024 in dev, otherwise the page origin; the production web build uses base /ui/ and outputs into the Python server package's static directory, which the server mounts at /ui.

packages/chess-ui is a private package whose exports point at TypeScript source (src/index.ts, styles.css, testing.ts) with no build step, so consuming apps compile it and must include its source in their Tailwind content globs and import its stylesheet.

chess-ui's ChessValues lists the only thread channels a UI may read (messages, start_fen, moves, plies, turns, outcome, error, and the optional setup); positions are rebuilt client-side by replaying moves, stopping silently at the first move chess.js rejects because the server is authoritative.

liveAnalysis returns the latest AI text after the current turn opened (or after the last human message), skipping AI messages already committed as a ply's message, so a previous move's analysis is never shown as live.

apps/review is built as a single dependency-free CommonJS bundle exporting render(data, container, metadata) for the LangSmith custom-app sandbox, with code splitting disabled and NODE_ENV defined as production outside Vitest; render creates the root, stylesheet and api dependencies once and re-renders in place so host updates do not reset loads.

The review app talks only to the LangSmith API through window.langsmith.call: it lists projects, queries threads by project and time window in pages of 20, then fetches the threads' last root runs and their game_review and grade_status feedback in parallel and joins them into games.

reviewsByRun only considers feedback with key game_review, a run_id, and feedback_source metadata grader 'lcchess grade' (other feedback under the key is ignored), and parseReview classifies it as graded only for a complete version-1 review with well-formed evals and ply grades and one eval per position, otherwise as invalid with the first problem found.

A review game's values are the last root run's outputs only when they validate as a game record (a UCI moves array plus well-shaped optional start_fen, plies, turns and outcome); otherwise the app shows 'No game record', and ungraded games show a 'Not graded yet' banner offering Analyze or lcchess grade --thread.

GameView marks move-list entries with graded quality, draws the played move and the engine's differing best move as arrows, and shows an eval bar, grade card and eval graph from a graded review's per-position evals; for invalid reviews AnalysisBanner shows 'Review unreadable' offering Re-analyze or a forced lcchess grade regrade.
The review App tags each loaded games page with its project and since query so a stale response is never displayed for a newer query.

The pnpm workspace contains apps/web, apps/review, evals/reports and packages/*, with shared dependency versions pinned in a catalog (vite aliased to vite-plus-core) and referenced as catalog: so packages cannot drift.

Lint and format are configured only in the root vite.config.ts because Vite+ ignores nested lint/fmt blocks; lint is type-aware oxlint with rules-of-hooks and prefer-vite-plus-imports, and formatting ignores apps/server, libs, the Python parts of evals, openwiki and the generated chess-ui settings.

The web and review apps run jsdom Vitest over tests/**/*.test.{ts,tsx} with 100% line, function, branch and statement coverage thresholds; the review app writes coverage outside its directory because langsmith apps push ignores .gitignore.

Web tests replace useStream with a shared fake that records options, supports per-thread overrides and simulates thread-load outcomes, a separate suite exercises useGame on the real SDK over stubbed fetch, and App accepts injectable random, checkKey and modelLimit so tests are deterministic without a server.

The New game dialog asks the server for the chosen LLM's input limit via GET /ui/model-limit (debounced 300 ms, sending x-api-key when set); a numeric max_input_tokens is known, null means the model has no known limit, and non-OK responses, malformed bodies and network errors are 'failed'; the Summarize memory option is disabled only for models with no known limit, a failed check blocks a game with memory on and offers Retry, and late answers for a no-longer-selected model are ignored.

The server's GameSetupMiddleware records the run's resolved ChessContext in a public, client-unwritable `setup` state channel only in the run that opened the game's first turn (both before and after the agent so failed or game-ending first turns still get it), never overwrites it, and never adds it to threads created before it existed.

The web UI continues a game from its thread: gameOf takes the context from the thread's `setup` only when loadRecorded accepts it (a valid version with exactly that version's keys, each valid, migrated to the current version), falls back to a new game's chosen context before its first turn is recorded, and otherwise yields no record so the game is view-only.

The human's side of a continued game is derived from the thread: the side of the last external ply, else the opposite of whoever played ply 0, else the picked side, else the side not to move in the start position.

useGame tracks each thread load by the SDK hydration promise as loading, missing (a clean load for a thread id that binds no thread), failed (rejected load) or ready, ignores superseded loads settling late, and the Table shows a Reload banner for failed loads and a not-on-server banner for missing threads while keeping the board locked.

The web app tolerates blocked localStorage: browserStorage returns null when storage access throws, writers report whether a save landed, and App shows a 'This browser isn't saving' banner when storage is blocked or a save fails.
The review app marks a graded review invalid when its ply UCIs do not match the game's moves, so evaluations are never drawn against a different move sequence.

The web build has two inputs, index.html (the play UI) and render.html (LangSmith's custom output renderer for the positions dataset, served at /ui/render.html), and gives Vite's preload helper its own chunk so render.html does not download the LangChain chunk.

The renderer's useParentMessage accepts a postMessage only when the page is embedded and the event source is the embedding window (trusting the parent window rather than an origin, since self-hosted LangSmith can be on any origin) and keeps the latest message readMessage can read.

readMessage ignores (returns null for) anything that is not an `output` or `reference` message; otherwise it builds the position from metadata.inputs (a valid start_fen and legally replaying moves plus legal moves) and returns a Stockfish reference (evals for every ranked move), a System 1 output (ranked moves with confidence and margin, or a failed ranking with its error), or `unreadable` with the first reason.

The renderer draws a locked chess-ui Board from the mover's side with the top three moves as arrows, next to a Stockfish eval table or System 1's top moves with confidence, margin, tournament, requests and latency, and follows the system colour scheme rather than the play UI's stored theme because LangSmith sends none.

The renderer URL is set on the positions dataset by `lcchess-evals positions upload --renderer-url`, which writes it into the dataset's iframe_config and requires an absolute https URL; render-preview.html is a dev-only page that is not a build input.

The New game dialog's Import reads a JSON file and loads it with chess-ui's loadSettings (version required and not newer than the app's, unknown keys and invalid values rejected, resolved over the defaults), replacing pickers and knobs while keeping the picked side, and shows the error as 'Couldn't import that setup' otherwise.

Export downloads opponent.json containing configurableOf(context), the same object a run sends as configurable; in the New game dialog it is enabled only while the matchup is playable, and a game's opponent card exports the game's recorded context.

chess-ui's generated/settings.ts (with settings.schema.json and opponent.schema.json) is written by `mise run generate:settings` from the Python ChessContext via langchain_chess_server.codegen, holding the settings version, types, specs, labels, help, defaults, per-version defaults and model_kwargs rules; it must not be hand-edited because a server test fails when committed files are stale.

chess-ui's settings.ts hand-mirrors the Python settings loading (version checks, migrations, loadSettings, loadRecorded, model_kwargs rules) and its tests run the shared cases in libs/systemone/tests/fixtures/settings-cases.json so the TypeScript and Python loaders agree.

The review app's Analyze writes a grade_status 'analyzing' feedback mark, creates a per-thread sandbox from the langchain-chess-grader snapshot with explicit delegated permissions, waits for it to be ready and launches a detached `lcchess grade ... --sandbox-job`; on launch failure it deletes the mark and sandbox and reports a readable reason, and the per-thread sandbox name makes a second start conflict rather than run twice.

The review app reads this grader's newest grade_status mark per run; an analyzing mark older than 10 minutes is treated as stalled, a failed mark carries the job's log, and retrying a failed or stalled job first deletes the old sandbox and mark.
